# Introduction

The aim of this vignette is to compare the covariance estimators available for PoSIRd.

We consider three estimators:

- pooled covariance based on residuals from the estimated segmentation:
  \[
  \hat{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{pool}}
  =
  \frac{1}{n-K}
  \sum_{k=1}^K
  \sum_{i\in I_k}
  (X_i-\hat{\mu}_k)(X_i-\hat{\mu}_k)^\top;
  \]

- first-difference estimator with entrywise median aggregation:
  \[
  \hat{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{EW}}
  =
  \left[
  \operatorname{median}_{b=1,\ldots,B}
  \left\{
  (\hat{\Sigma}_b)_{j\ell}
  \right\}
  \right]_{j,\ell=1}^d,
  \qquad
  \hat{\Sigma}_b
  =
  \frac{1}{2|I_b|}
  \sum_{i\in I_b}
  \Delta_i\Delta_i^\top,
  \quad
  \Delta_i=X_{i+1}-X_i;
  \]

- first-difference estimator with geometric-median aggregation:
  \[
  \hat{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{GM}}
  =
  \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{M\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}}
  \sum_{b=1}^B
  \|\hat{\Sigma}_b-M\|_F,
  \]
  where \(\hat{\Sigma}_b\) is defined as above.
The pooled estimator uses the supplied segmentation and is therefore expected to perform well when the segmentation is correct, but may be affected by missed changepoints.

The first-difference estimators do not use the segmentation. They estimate the
covariance from consecutive differences and use robust aggregation to reduce
the effect of differences crossing true changepoints.

We investigate:

- estimation error with respect to the true covariance matrix;
- eigenvalues and condition number of the estimators;
- frequency with which the raw MoM estimators are not positive definite;
- sensitivity to correct segmentation, undersegmentation and
  oversegmentation.

```{r}
library(mvtnorm)
```

# Simulation parameters

We consider a two-dimensional Gaussian piecewise-constant signal

\[
X_i = \mu_i + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad
\varepsilon_i \sim N(0,\Sigma),
\]

with

\[
\Sigma =
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & \rho \\
\rho & 1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

```{r}
Qtable_path <- here::here(

)

message("Quantile path: ", Qtable_path)

Qtable <- read_quantiles(

```

```{r}
n <- 1000
n_chg <- 10
n_segments <- n_chg + 1

delta <- 0.05
alpha <- 0.05

rho <- 0.5
Sigma <- matrix(
  c(
    1, rho,
    rho, 1
  ),
  nrow = 2
)

possible_states <- c(
  -2,
  0,
  2
)

n_sim <- 1000

covariance_blocks <- 10L
```

# Generate changepoints and signal

We generate changepoints under the constraint that every true segment has
length at least $n\delta$.

```{r}
generate_changepoints <- function(
    n,
    n_chg,
    delta
) {
  n_segments <- n_chg + 1L
  min_length <- ceiling(delta * n)

  remaining_length <-
    n - n_segments * min_length

  if (remaining_length < 0L) {
    stop(
      "The requested number of changepoints is incompatible with delta."
    )
  }

  segment_lengths <- min_length +
    as.vector(
      rmultinom(
        n = 1,
        size = remaining_length,
        prob = rep(1, n_segments)
      )
    )

  changepoints <- cumsum(
    segment_lengths
  )[-n_segments]

  list(
    changepoints = changepoints,
    lengths = segment_lengths
  )
}
```

Generate segment means, requiring the mean to change in both coordinates at
every changepoint.

```{r}
generate_means <- function(
    n_segments,
    possible_states
) {
  means <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_segments,
    ncol = 2
  )

  means[1, ] <- sample(
    possible_states,
    size = 2,
    replace = TRUE
  )

  for (i in 2:n_segments) {
    means[i, 1] <- sample(
      setdiff(
        possible_states,
        means[i - 1, 1]
      ),
      size = 1
    )

    means[i, 2] <- sample(
      setdiff(
        possible_states,
        means[i - 1, 2]
      ),
      size = 1
    )
  }

  colnames(means) <- c(
    "mu1",
    "mu2"
  )

  means
}
```

Generate observations.

```{r}
generate_data <- function(
    n,
    changepoints,
    means,
    Sigma
) {
  boundaries <- c(
    0,
    changepoints,
    n
  )

  x <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n,
    ncol = 2
  )

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(means))) {
    current_rows <-
      (boundaries[i] + 1L):boundaries[i + 1L]

    x[current_rows, ] <- rmvnorm(
      n = length(current_rows),
      mean = means[i, ],
      sigma = Sigma
    )
  }

  colnames(x) <- c(
    "Y1",
    "Y2"
  )

  x
}
```

# Segmentation scenarios

We consider three situations.

## Correct segmentation

The pooled estimator receives the true changepoints.

## Undersegmentation

We remove every second true changepoint. Therefore, some estimated segments
contain multiple true means.

```{r}
undersegment <- function(
    true_changepoints
) {
  true_changepoints[
    seq(
      2L,
      length(true_changepoints),
      by = 2L
    )
  ]
}
```

## Oversegmentation

We add a changepoint at the midpoint of every true segment whenever possible.

```{r}
oversegment <- function(
    true_changepoints,
    n
) {
  boundaries <- c(
    0,
    true_changepoints,
    n
  )

  additional_changepoints <- vapply(
    seq_len(length(boundaries) - 1L),
    function(i) {
      as.integer(
        floor(
          (
            boundaries[i] +
            boundaries[i + 1L]
          ) / 2
        )
      )
    },
    integer(1)
  )

  sort(
    unique(
      c(
        true_changepoints,
        additional_changepoints
      )
    )
  )
}
```

# Helper functions

## Segment means and lengths

```{r}
get_segment_information <- function(
    x,
    breakpoints
) {
  n <- nrow(x)

  boundaries <- c(
    0,
    breakpoints,
    n
  )

  lengths <- diff(boundaries)

  means <- t(
    vapply(
      seq_len(length(lengths)),
      function(i) {
        current_rows <-
          (boundaries[i] + 1L):boundaries[i + 1L]

        colMeans(
          x[
            current_rows,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
        )
      },
      numeric(ncol(x))
    )
  )

  list(
    means = means,
    lengths = lengths
  )
}
```

## Raw first-difference estimators

For this simulation we need the covariance estimates *before* the
positive-definite correction, because we want to record how often each
aggregation method naturally produces a non-PD matrix.

```{r}
estimate_covariance_diff_mom_raw <- function(
    x,
    number_of_blocks,
    aggregation = c(
      "entrywise",
      "geometric"
    )
) {
  aggregation <- match.arg(
    aggregation
  )

  n <- nrow(x)

  first_differences <-
    x[-1L, , drop = FALSE] -
    x[-n, , drop = FALSE]

  block_indices <- split_into_consecutive_blocks(
    number_of_observations = n - 1L,
    number_of_blocks = number_of_blocks
  )

  block_covariances <- lapply(
    block_indices,
    function(indices) {
      current_differences <-
        first_differences[
          indices,
          ,
          drop = FALSE
        ]

      crossprod(
        current_differences
      ) / (
        2 * length(indices)
      )
    }
  )

  switch(
    aggregation,

    entrywise = {
      entrywise_matrix_median(
        block_covariances
      )
    },

    geometric = {
      geometric_matrix_median(
        block_covariances
      )
    }
  )
}
```

## Covariance diagnostics

```{r}
covariance_diagnostics <- function(
    covariance,
    true_covariance
) {
  eigenvalues <- eigen(
    covariance,
    symmetric = TRUE,
    only.values = TRUE
  )$values

  difference <-
    covariance - true_covariance

  frobenius_error <- sqrt(
    sum(difference^2)
  )

  relative_frobenius_error <-
    frobenius_error /
    sqrt(sum(true_covariance^2))

  operator_error <- max(
    abs(
      eigen(
        difference,
        symmetric = TRUE,
        only.values = TRUE
      )$values
    )
  )

  true_operator_norm <- max(
    abs(
      eigen(
        true_covariance,
        symmetric = TRUE,
        only.values = TRUE
      )$values
    )
  )

  relative_operator_error <-
    operator_error /
    true_operator_norm

  list(
    relative_frobenius_error =
      relative_frobenius_error,
    relative_operator_error =
      relative_operator_error,
    minimum_eigenvalue =
      min(eigenvalues),
    maximum_eigenvalue =
      max(eigenvalues),
    condition_number =
      if (min(eigenvalues) > 0) {
        max(eigenvalues) /
          min(eigenvalues)
      } else {
        Inf
      },
    positive_definite =
      all(eigenvalues > 0)
  )
}
```

# One simulation

Before running the full experiment, inspect the three estimators in one
simulation.

```{r}
set.seed(1418)

segmentation <- generate_changepoints(
  n = n,
  n_chg = n_chg,
  delta = delta
)

true_chg <- segmentation$changepoints

true_means <- generate_means(
  n_segments = n_segments,
  possible_states = possible_states
)

x <- generate_data(
  n = n,
  changepoints = true_chg,
  means = true_means,
  Sigma = Sigma
)

under_chg <- undersegment(
  true_chg
)

over_chg <- oversegment(
  true_changepoints = true_chg,
  n = n
)
```

Compute the pooled estimator under the three segmentations.

```{r}
pooled_estimates <- lapply(
  list(
    correct = true_chg,
    under = under_chg,
    over = over_chg
  ),
  function(breakpoints) {
    segment_information <-
      get_segment_information(
        x = x,
        breakpoints = breakpoints
      )

    estimate_covariance_pooled(
      x = x,
      means = segment_information$means,
      lengths = segment_information$lengths
    )
  }
)

pooled_estimates
```

The two first-difference estimators do not depend on the supplied
segmentation.

```{r}
cov_entrywise_raw <-
  estimate_covariance_diff_mom_raw(
    x = x,
    number_of_blocks = covariance_blocks,
    aggregation = "entrywise"
  )

cov_geometric_raw <-
  estimate_covariance_diff_mom_raw(
    x = x,
    number_of_blocks = covariance_blocks,
    aggregation = "geometric"
  )

cov_entrywise_raw
cov_geometric_raw
```

Compare them with the true covariance.

```{r}
Sigma

covariance_diagnostics(
  pooled_estimates$correct,
  Sigma
)

covariance_diagnostics(
  pooled_estimates$under,
  Sigma
)

covariance_diagnostics(
  pooled_estimates$over,
  Sigma
)

covariance_diagnostics(
  cov_entrywise_raw,
  Sigma
)

covariance_diagnostics(
  cov_geometric_raw,
  Sigma
)
```

# Simulation study

We now repeat the experiment and record the estimation error and spectral
properties of each estimator.

```{r}
set.seed(1442)

segmentation_methods <- c(
  "correct",
  "under",
  "over"
)

covariance_methods <- c(
  "pooled",
  "diff_mom_entrywise",
  "diff_mom_geometric"
)

results <- vector(
  "list",
  n_sim * (
    length(segmentation_methods) +
    2L
  )
)

result_index <- 1L

for (sim in seq_len(n_sim)) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Generate signal
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  segmentation <- generate_changepoints(
    n = n,
    n_chg = n_chg,
    delta = delta
  )

  true_chg <- segmentation$changepoints

  true_means <- generate_means(
    n_segments = n_chg + 1L,
    possible_states = possible_states
  )

  x <- generate_data(
    n = n,
    changepoints = true_chg,
    means = true_means,
    Sigma = Sigma
  )

  segmentations <- list(
    correct = true_chg,
    under = undersegment(
      true_chg
    ),
    over = oversegment(
      true_changepoints = true_chg,
      n = n
    )
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pooled estimator
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  for (
    segmentation_name in names(segmentations)
  ) {
    current_chg <-
      segmentations[[segmentation_name]]

    segment_information <-
      get_segment_information(
        x = x,
        breakpoints = current_chg
      )

    covariance_raw <-
      estimate_covariance_pooled(
        x = x,
        means = segment_information$means,
        lengths = segment_information$lengths
      )

    diagnostics <-
      covariance_diagnostics(
        covariance = covariance_raw,
        true_covariance = Sigma
      )

    results[[result_index]] <- data.frame(
      simulation = sim,
      covariance_method = "pooled",
      segmentation = segmentation_name,
      relative_frobenius_error =
        diagnostics$relative_frobenius_error,
      relative_operator_error =
        diagnostics$relative_operator_error,
      minimum_eigenvalue =
        diagnostics$minimum_eigenvalue,
      maximum_eigenvalue =
        diagnostics$maximum_eigenvalue,
      condition_number =
        diagnostics$condition_number,
      raw_positive_definite =
        diagnostics$positive_definite
    )

    result_index <- result_index + 1L
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # First-difference estimators
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  for (
    aggregation in c(
      "entrywise",
      "geometric"
    )
  ) {
    covariance_raw <-
      estimate_covariance_diff_mom_raw(
        x = x,
        number_of_blocks = covariance_blocks,
        aggregation = aggregation
      )

    diagnostics <-
      covariance_diagnostics(
        covariance = covariance_raw,
        true_covariance = Sigma
      )

    results[[result_index]] <- data.frame(
      simulation = sim,
      covariance_method = paste0(
        "diff_mom_",
        aggregation
      ),
      segmentation = "independent",
      relative_frobenius_error =
        diagnostics$relative_frobenius_error,
      relative_operator_error =
        diagnostics$relative_operator_error,
      minimum_eigenvalue =
        diagnostics$minimum_eigenvalue,
      maximum_eigenvalue =
        diagnostics$maximum_eigenvalue,
      condition_number =
        diagnostics$condition_number,
      raw_positive_definite =
        diagnostics$positive_definite
    )

    result_index <- result_index + 1L
  }

  if (sim %% 100L == 0L) {
    message(
      "Simulation ",
      sim,
      "/",
      n_sim
    )
  }
}

simulation_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  results
)

rownames(simulation_results) <- NULL
```

# Estimation error

## Relative Frobenius error

```{r}
aggregate(
  relative_frobenius_error ~
    covariance_method + segmentation,
  data = simulation_results,

      median = median(x),
      q90 = quantile(x, 0.90)
```

```{r}
)
```

# Positive definiteness

We now examine the raw covariance estimates, before applying
`make_positive_definite()`.

```{r}
pd_summary <- aggregate(
  raw_positive_definite ~
    covariance_method + segmentation,
  data = simulation_results,
  FUN = mean
)

pd_summary$non_pd_frequency <-
  1 - pd_summary$raw_positive_definite

pd_summary
```

In particular, the frequencies for the two first-difference estimators are

```{r}
subset(
  pd_summary,
  covariance_method %in% c(
    "diff_mom_entrywise",
    "diff_mom_geometric"
  )
)
```

# PoSIRd coverage and confidence-region area

We now investigate how the three covariance estimators affect PoSIRd
confidence regions.

For each simulated data set we consider:

- correct segmentation;
- undersegmentation;
- oversegmentation.

For each segmentation, we compute PoSIRd confidence regions using:

- pooled covariance;
- entrywise MoM covariance;
- geometric-median MoM covariance.

For an arbitrary supplied segment, the target parameter is the mean of the
true signal over that segment.

# True signal and targets

## True signal at every observation

```{r}
get_true_signal <- function(
    n,
    true_changepoints,
    true_means
) {
  boundaries <- c(
    0L,
    true_changepoints,
    n
  )

  true_signal <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n,
    ncol = ncol(true_means)
  )

  for (
    segment
    in seq_len(
      nrow(true_means)
    )
  ) {
    current_rows <- (
      boundaries[segment] + 1L
    ):boundaries[segment + 1L]

    true_signal[
      current_rows,
    ] <- matrix(
      true_means[segment, ],
      nrow =
        length(current_rows),
      ncol =
        ncol(true_means),
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  }

  colnames(true_signal) <-
    colnames(true_means)

  true_signal
}
```

## True target associated with a supplied segmentation

```{r}
get_true_targets <- function(
    true_signal,
    breakpoints
) {
  n <- nrow(
    true_signal
  )

  boundaries <- c(
    0L,
    breakpoints,
    n
  )

  number_of_segments <-
    length(boundaries) - 1L

  targets <- t(
    vapply(
      seq_len(
        number_of_segments
      ),
      function(segment) {
        current_rows <- (
          boundaries[segment] + 1L
        ):boundaries[segment + 1L]

        colMeans(
          true_signal[
            current_rows,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
        )
      },
      numeric(
        ncol(true_signal)
      )
    )
  )

  colnames(targets) <-
    colnames(true_signal)

  targets
}
```

# Construct PoSIRd regions with a chosen covariance estimator

The PoSIRd quantile, estimated means, segment lengths and validity are obtained
from `confidence_regions_1D()`. We then use the desired covariance estimator.

```{r}
get_posird_regions <- function(
    x,
    breakpoints,
    covariance_method,
    delta,
    alpha,
    Qtable,
    covariance_blocks
) {
  covariance_method <- match.arg(
    covariance_method,
    c(
      "pooled",
      "diff_mom_entrywise",
      "diff_mom_geometric"
    )
  )

  regions <- confidence_regions_1D(
    x = x,
    breakpoints = breakpoints,
    delta = delta,
    alpha = alpha,
    Qtable = Qtable
  )

  covariance <- switch(
    covariance_method,

    pooled = {
      estimate_covariance_pooled(
        x = x,
        means = regions$means,
        lengths = regions$lengths
      )
    },

    diff_mom_entrywise = {
      estimate_covariance_diff_mom(
        x = x,
        number_of_blocks =
          covariance_blocks,
        aggregation =
          "entrywise"
      )
    },

    diff_mom_geometric = {
      estimate_covariance_diff_mom(
        x = x,
        number_of_blocks =
          covariance_blocks,
        aggregation =
          "geometric"
      )
    }
  )

  regions$covariance <-
    covariance

  regions
}
```

# Evaluate coverage and ellipse area

For segment \(k\), coverage is evaluated using

\[
n_k
(\widehat\mu_k-\mu_k)^\top
\widehat\Sigma^{-1}
(\widehat\mu_k-\mu_k)
\leq q^2.
\]

For a two-dimensional signal, the area of the corresponding confidence ellipse
is

\[
\pi
\frac{q^2}{n_k}
\sqrt{\det(\widehat\Sigma)}.
\]

```{r}
evaluate_posird_regions <- function(
    regions,
    true_targets
) {
  number_of_segments <-
    nrow(
      regions$means
    )

  if (
    nrow(true_targets) !=
      number_of_segments
  ) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "The number of true targets",
        "does not match the number",
        "of supplied segments."
      )
    )
  }

  segment_coverage <- rep(
    NA,
    number_of_segments
  )

  areas <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    number_of_segments
  )

  critical_value <-
    regions$quantile^2

  covariance_factor <- sqrt(
    det(
      regions$covariance
    )
  )

  for (
    segment
    in seq_len(
      number_of_segments
    )
  ) {

    if (
      !regions$valid[segment]
    ) {
      next
    }

    distance_squared <- mahalanobis(
      x = matrix(
        true_targets[
          segment,
        ],
        nrow = 1L
      ),
      center =
        regions$means[
          segment,
        ],
      cov =
        regions$covariance
    )

    statistic <-
      regions$lengths[segment] *
      distance_squared

    segment_coverage[segment] <-
      statistic <=
      critical_value

    areas[segment] <-
      pi *
      critical_value /
      regions$lengths[segment] *
      covariance_factor
  }

  valid_coverage <-
    segment_coverage[
      regions$valid
    ]

  valid_areas <-
    areas[
      regions$valid
    ]

  list(
    segment_coverage =
      segment_coverage,

    simultaneous_coverage =
      all(valid_coverage),

    mean_area =
      mean(
        valid_areas
      ),

    median_area =
      median(
        valid_areas
      ),

    minimum_area =
      min(
        valid_areas
      ),

    maximum_area =
      max(
        valid_areas
      ),

    n_segments =
      number_of_segments,

    n_valid_segments =
      sum(
        regions$valid
      )
  )
}
```

# Monte Carlo evaluation of PoSIRd

For this experiment, we keep the same underlying signal across Monte Carlo
replicates and generate new Gaussian noise, as in the previous PoSIRd
coverage simulation.

```{r}
oversegment <- function(
    true_changepoints,
    n,
    delta
) {
  boundaries <- c(
    0L,
    true_changepoints,
    n
  )

  minimum_length <- ceiling(
    delta * n
  )

  additional_changepoints <- integer(0)

  for (
    segment in seq_len(
      length(boundaries) - 1L
    )
  ) {
    left <- boundaries[segment]
    right <- boundaries[segment + 1L]

    segment_length <- right - left

    if (segment_length >= 2L * minimum_length) {
      midpoint <- as.integer(
        floor(
          (left + right) / 2
        )
      )

      if (
        midpoint - left >= minimum_length &&
        right - midpoint >= minimum_length
      ) {
        additional_changepoints <- c(
          additional_changepoints,
          midpoint
        )
      }
    }
  }

  sort(
    unique(
      c(
        true_changepoints,
        additional_changepoints
      )
    )
  )
}

n_sim_posird <- 1000

covariance_methods <- c(
  "pooled",
  "diff_mom_entrywise",
  "diff_mom_geometric"
)

segmentation_methods <- c(
  "correct",
  "under",
  "over"
)

true_signal <- get_true_signal(
  n = n,
  true_changepoints =
    true_chg,
  true_means =
    true_means
)

fixed_segmentations <- list(
  correct =
    true_chg,

  under =
    undersegment(
      true_chg
    ),

  over =
    oversegment(
      true_changepoints =
        true_chg,
      n = n,
      delta = delta
    )
)

fixed_targets <- lapply(
  fixed_segmentations,
  function(breakpoints) {
    get_true_targets(
      true_signal =
        true_signal,
      breakpoints =
        breakpoints
    )
  }
)
```

```{r}
set.seed(1528)

posird_results <- vector(
  "list",
  n_sim_posird *
    length(
      covariance_methods
    ) *
    length(
      segmentation_methods
    )
)

result_index <- 1L

for (
  sim
  in seq_len(
    n_sim_posird
  )
) {

  # Generate a new data set with the same signal
  x <- generate_data(
    n = n,
    changepoints =
      true_chg,
    means =
      true_means,
    Sigma =
      Sigma
  )

  for (
    segmentation_name
    in names(
      fixed_segmentations
    )
  ) {

    current_breakpoints <-
      fixed_segmentations[[segmentation_name]]

    current_targets <-
      fixed_targets[[segmentation_name]]

    for (
      covariance_method
      in covariance_methods
    ) {

      regions <-
        get_posird_regions(
          x = x,
          breakpoints =
            current_breakpoints,
          covariance_method =
            covariance_method,
          delta = delta,
          alpha = alpha,
          Qtable = Qtable,
          covariance_blocks =
            covariance_blocks
        )

      evaluation <-
        evaluate_posird_regions(
          regions =
            regions,
          true_targets =
            current_targets
        )

      posird_results[[result_index]] <- data.frame(
        simulation =
          sim,

        segmentation =
          segmentation_name,

        covariance_method =
          covariance_method,

        simultaneous_coverage =
          evaluation$
            simultaneous_coverage,

        mean_area =
          evaluation$
            mean_area,

        median_area =
          evaluation$
            median_area,

        minimum_area =
          evaluation$
            minimum_area,

        maximum_area =
          evaluation$
            maximum_area,

        n_segments =
          evaluation$
            n_segments,

        n_valid_segments =
          evaluation$
            n_valid_segments
      )

      result_index <-
        result_index + 1L
    }
  }

  if (
    sim %% 100L == 0L
  ) {
    message(
      "PoSIRd simulation ",
      sim,
      "/",
      n_sim_posird
    )
  }
}

posird_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  posird_results
)

rownames(
  posird_results
) <- NULL
```

# Relative area with respect to the correct pooled estimator

To make the magnitude of the differences easier to interpret, compare each
configuration with the mean area obtained using the pooled estimator under the
correct segmentation.

```{r}
reference_area <- mean(
  posird_results$mean_area[
    posird_results$segmentation ==
      "correct" &
    posird_results$covariance_method ==
      "pooled"
  ]
)

posird_results$relative_area <-
  posird_results$mean_area /
  reference_area
```

```{r}
final_summary
```

# Interpretation

The most important comparison is the undersegmentation scenario.

When true changepoints are missed, the pooled residual covariance estimator
contains residual variation due to changes in the signal mean. We therefore
expect the pooled covariance estimate to become inflated, particularly in the
directions corresponding to the missed jumps.

This inflation may not necessarily cause undercoverage. Instead, it can lead to
larger PoSIRd confidence ellipses and therefore conservative simultaneous
coverage.

The first-difference estimators are independent of the supplied segmentation,
so their covariance estimates are unchanged across the three segmentation
scenarios for a fixed data set. However, the PoSIRd regions still depend on the
segmentation through the estimated segment means, lengths and target
parameters.

The coverage results should therefore always be interpreted together with the
ellipse areas.
